title: Say which gate role's confinement is enforced and which is instructional, and record the measurement that settles it

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 43, round 1. Audited commit eaac731 (on a08dbf5, the sprint start). The sprint file was read fresh at HEAD and is unchanged since a08dbf5. Verdict: CONDITIONAL. The sprint's purpose is to stop these files implying more than holds, and the new qa1.md text does exactly that in a configuration the sprint did not consider. Everything else is met.

REQUIRED FIX.
1. [MEDIUM] Req 2: qa1.md's enforced-confinement claim is stated unconditionally, but it only holds when the repository is NOT declared as owned.
 - qa1's profile carries eligibleForOwnedRepositoryGrant: true. When .claude/settings.local.json declares "fullyCompletely.ownedRepository", resolveOwnedRepositoryGrant splices OWNED_REPOSITORY_ALLOWED_TOOLS into qa1's allowedTools, and that list contains Bash(npm *), Bash(npx *), Bash(node *), Bash(bash *), Bash(sh *), Bash(git *) among others.
 - Demonstrated at eaac731: in a scratch repo with that declaration present, headlessPermissionArgs for qa1 returns an allowedTools string that holds Bash(node *): true, Bash(npx *): true, Bash(git *): true.
 - So these sentences in qa1.md are false in that configuration: "Your headless profile holds no Bash(node *), no Bash(npx *)"; "for you, this boundary IS enforced by the tool layer, not merely an instruction you follow"; "it is narrow enough that the tool layer itself -- not just your own restraint -- actually holds you to it". Under a declared-owned repo the very probe the file cites as DENIED would be granted, by the same reasoning the file itself applies to LiveQA (a node * grant reaches a child process and therefore git).
 - This is the sprint's own stated failure mode. Context says "Both files currently imply more uniformity than holds"; the fix must not replace that with implying more enforcement than holds.
 - Suggested fix: qualify the claim where it is made -- enforced under the default headless profile, and explicitly NOT enforced when the operator has declared this repository as owned (sprint 19's grant), with one line saying what a QA1 session should do about it (treat the rule as instructional in that case, exactly as LiveQA does). CLAUDE.md's new paragraph says QA1 "holds no arbitrary-execution primitive at all" and needs the same qualification.
 - Also in that paragraph: "your grant is the narrowest of the six roles" is not accurate. master-controller holds the same three entries, is NOT eligible for the owned-repository grant, and has no test-command grant; qa1 has both. Either drop the superlative or make it "narrowest among the roles that run code".
2. [LOW] Same sentence: "no route to a child process" is literally false even on the default profile. qa1 holds Bash(node scripts/run-lifecycle.js *), Bash(python3 scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py *) and Bash(node scripts/gate-commit.js *), and gate-commit.js itself spawns git. The intended claim is "no route to an ARBITRARY child process", which is both true and the point. Worth fixing in the same edit, since sprint 42's wrapper is precisely a narrow, sanctioned child process and this file documents it elsewhere.
3. [LOW] Req 6: the new test only exercises the default profile, so it cannot catch the case in item 1. Add an assertion for the declared-owned path -- either that qa1 under an ownership declaration is documented as an exception, or (better) that the documentation and the grant agree in both configurations. A test that guards only the configuration where the claim is already true is the same shape of gap as the claim itself.

WHAT IS FINE.
 - Req 1: liveqa.md states plainly that its confinement is instructional, names the unconstrained routes (node/npx to a child process, and therefore git and file writes), gives the reason (its job is running published artifacts), cites the measurement at claude 2.1.278, and explicitly ties it to the existing never-write-source rule so it reads as that principle extended rather than a new licence. It also correctly reframes gate-commit.js as a convenience for LiveQA rather than a boundary.
 - Req 3: the findings entry carries the version anchor (claude 2.1.278), the method (two real headless launches, same scratch project, identical node -e probe per profile, verdict from permission_denials plus real git state, never narration), a per-profile outcome table, and the relationship to sprint 39 (confirms rather than contradicts: node * widened nothing because npx * already reached that far). It is sourced from LiveQA's own recorded sprint 42 verdict rather than reconstructed.
 - Req 4: scripts/launcher/run-role.js is not in the diff at all, so HEADLESS_PERMISSION_PROFILES is byte-unchanged and no grant moved. The only script touched is launcher_test.js.
 - Req 5: CLAUDE.md's new paragraph does state the general principle (a role whose job is running arbitrary code cannot be confined by tool grants; state the rule as an instruction and verify by review), not merely this instance -- subject to item 1's qualification about QA1.
 - Req 6, as far as it goes: I planted four grant changes against the new test in a clean clone at eaac731, each reverted after:
   - qa1 granted Bash(node *): FAILS (three tests, including two pre-existing profile guards).
   - qa1 granted Bash(npx *): FAILS (three tests).
   - qa1's disallowedTools emptied (Edit/Write re-enabled): FAILS the new test.
   - liveqa stripped of both node * and npx *: FAILS the new test, which is the right behaviour in the other direction too.
   So the test is real, and its failure messages name the documentation claim rather than just the grant.
 - No version bump: package.json is untouched, as the sprint's own header requires.
 - Both suites pass at eaac731: node scripts/launcher_test.js ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, bash scripts/smoke_test.sh ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED.

FOR MASTER CONTROLLER, not a Dev Team item. The sprint file's own Req 2 states the enforced claim unconditionally too ("No node */npx *, Edit/Write denied"), so the premise carries the same gap as the text it asked for. Worth a one-line amendment recording the owned-repository exception, so the record matches what ships. This is not blocking the fix above.

FOR LIVEQA, when this eventually ships. Re-confirm both probes on the CLI version current at that time, and add the declared-owned configuration to the QA1 side: with an ownership declaration present, the node -e probe should be expected to RUN, and the documentation should say so.

CONDITIONAL: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 43, round 2. Audited commit 8836924. The sprint file was re-read and is unchanged since a08dbf5. Verdict: CONDITIONAL, for one wrong clause introduced by this fix round. All three round-1 findings are properly fixed. This sprint has no version bump and is held for a later release, so a third round costs no shipping time; I would rather it ship correct than ship with a false location for a security-relevant declaration.

REQUIRED FIX.
1. [LOW, but wrong in a sentence whose whole job is precision] qa1.md now says the ownership declaration lives in "`fullyCompletely.ownedRepository` in `.vscode/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json`". Only the second is read.
 - readOwnedRepositoryDeclaration (run-role.js, around line 1188) reads exactly one file: path.join(root, '.claude', 'settings.local.json'). There is no .vscode fallback anywhere in that function.
 - Demonstrated at 8836924: with the declaration placed ONLY in .vscode/settings.json, headlessPermissionArgs for qa1 does NOT gain Bash(node *) (false). With it in .claude/settings.local.json, it does (verified in round 1, and this sprint's own new test uses that path).
 - The failure direction matters: a QA1 session told to check .vscode/settings.json sees nothing there, concludes it is on the default profile, and believes a boundary that a declaration in the other file has already removed. That is precisely the wrong-way-round error this sprint exists to prevent.
 - Fix: name only `.claude/settings.local.json`. Your own new test already uses that path, so prose and test would then agree.
 - Note the same clause also says "the same declaration Dev Team's own broad grant uses", which is correct and worth keeping.

ROUND-1 FINDINGS, ALL FIXED.
 - [MEDIUM] The enforced-confinement claim is now explicitly conditional: DEFAULT profile enforced, and a declared-owned repository hands qa1 the identical broad set Dev Team gets (Bash(node *), Bash(npx *), Bash(git *), bash, sh), at which point the probe would run rather than be denied and the rule is instructional, same as LiveQA's. It also tells a QA1 session what to do in that case (treat it as instructional, say so in notes if it bears on a finding). CLAUDE.md's mirrored paragraph and the findings entry carry the same qualification.
 - [LOW] "no route to a child process" is now "no route to an *arbitrary* child process", with gate-commit.js named as the narrow, purpose-built exception. Accurate.
 - [LOW] The "narrowest of the six roles" overclaim is gone, replaced with an accurate comparison: Master Controller's default is the same three script grants and is never eligible for the broader one. Correct, and I checked it against the profiles rather than taking it on trust.
 - The new companion test covers the declared-owned case. Negative control, run by QA1: flipping qa1's eligibleForOwnedRepositoryGrant to false makes that test FAIL (along with two pre-existing profile guards). The round-1 test's four plantings still fail as before.

EVERYTHING ELSE STILL HOLDS AT 8836924.
 - Req 1: liveqa.md untouched this round, and correct as audited in round 1.
 - Req 3: the findings entry keeps its version anchor (claude 2.1.278), method, per-profile outcomes, and the sprint 39 relationship, now with the owned-repository qualification.
 - Req 4: scripts/launcher/run-role.js is still not in the sprint's diff at all, so HEADLESS_PERMISSION_PROFILES is byte-unchanged and no grant moved.
 - Req 5: CLAUDE.md states the general principle, now accurately qualified for QA1.
 - No version bump: package.json untouched across the whole sprint.
 - Req 6: both suites pass at 8836924. node scripts/launcher_test.js ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED; bash scripts/smoke_test.sh ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED.

FOR MASTER CONTROLLER, carried from round 1 and correctly relayed by Dev Team: sprint 43's own Req 2 still states the enforced claim unconditionally, so the premise carries the gap the text no longer does. A one-line amendment would make the record match what shipped. Not blocking.

FOR LIVEQA, when this eventually ships: re-confirm both probes on the CLI version current then, and add the declared-owned QA1 case (declaration in .claude/settings.local.json) where the node -e probe should RUN.

PASS: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 43, round 3. Audited commit ba39be3. The sprint file was re-read and is unchanged since a08dbf5. Verdict: PASS.

SCOPE. The delta 8836924..ba39be3 outside bookkeeping is one line of .claude/agents/qa1.md.

1. Round-2 finding (wrong settings file named): FIXED, and verified.
 - The clause now reads: fullyCompletely.ownedRepository in `.claude/settings.local.json` -- "that one file only, readOwnedRepositoryDeclaration() in run-role.js never reads .vscode/settings.json, no fallback exists -- the same declaration Dev Team's own broad grant uses".
 - That matches the code exactly (readOwnedRepositoryDeclaration opens path.join(root, '.claude', 'settings.local.json') and nothing else), and matches the path this sprint's own declared-owned test writes.
 - The only surviving mention of .vscode/settings.json in qa1.md is inside that correction, stating that the file is never read. That is accurate and worth keeping: it forecloses the wrong guess rather than leaving it open.
 - No other file carried the error, confirmed by grep across .claude/, CLAUDE.md and the findings doc.

2. Everything verified in rounds 1 and 2 still holds at ba39be3:
 - Req 1: liveqa.md states the instructional confinement, the unconstrained routes, the reason, and ties it to the existing never-write-source rule.
 - Req 2: qa1.md's enforced claim is properly conditional (DEFAULT profile enforced; declared-owned repo hands qa1 the same broad set Dev Team gets, at which point the rule is instructional), names gate-commit.js as the narrow sanctioned child process rather than claiming none exists, and drops the "narrowest of the six" overclaim for an accurate comparison with Master Controller.
 - Req 3: the findings entry carries the version anchor (claude 2.1.278), method, per-profile outcomes, the owned-repository qualification, and the sprint 39 relationship.
 - Req 4: scripts/launcher/run-role.js is not in this sprint's diff at all. The full sprint (a08dbf5..ba39be3) touches only .claude/agents/liveqa.md, .claude/agents/qa1.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/sprint-12-permission-scope-findings.md, scripts/launcher_test.js and the sprint's own state file. HEADLESS_PERMISSION_PROFILES is byte-unchanged and no grant moved.
 - Req 5: CLAUDE.md's general-principle paragraph is present and accurately qualified.
 - Req 6: the two tests (default profile, declared-owned companion) both exist and are real. Across rounds I planted six changes -- qa1 granted node *, qa1 granted npx *, qa1's disallowedTools emptied, liveqa stripped of both primitives, and qa1's eligibleForOwnedRepositoryGrant flipped to false -- and each failed the suite, with messages naming the documentation claim rather than just the grant.
 - No version bump: package.json is untouched across the whole sprint, as the header requires.

3. Suites at ba39be3 in a clean clone: node scripts/launcher_test.js ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, exit 0. bash scripts/smoke_test.sh ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, exit 0.

FOR MASTER CONTROLLER, carried and still open (not blocking this PASS): sprint 43's own Req 2 states the enforced claim unconditionally, so the sprint file's premise is now narrower than the text it produced. A one-line amendment would make the record match what shipped. Note that amending the sprint file after this PASS will require a fresh QA1 audit before /sprint-dev-done -- the hash check is doing its job, and this is a cheap re-audit if you decide the amendment is worth it.

FOR LIVEQA, when this reaches a published release: re-confirm both probes on the CLI version current at that time and record it; add the declared-owned QA1 case (declaration in .claude/settings.local.json) where the node -e probe should RUN rather than be denied. If either has changed, this documentation is stale and needs its own correction.

PASS: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 43, round 4. Audited commit 3471879. Verdict: PASS. Short round, as expected: this re-audit exists because Master Controller amended the sprint file after a PASS, which the dev-done hash check correctly requires a fresh audit for.

WHAT MOVED. Only the sprint file (3471879): Req 2's wording, and one added LiveQA criterion. Everything outside docs/sprints/ is byte-identical to ba39be3, which I passed in round 3 (git diff ba39be3..HEAD excluding docs/sprints is empty), so round 3's suite runs and code review carry over unchanged rather than being re-asserted here.

1. The amendment is accurate to what shipped, checked clause by clause against the current .claude/agents/qa1.md rather than against my memory of it:
 - Req 2's headline now states the enforcement conditionally ("enforced on its DEFAULT profile"), which matches the shipped text.
 - 2(a) gate-commit.js as a sanctioned, purpose-built narrow child process: present in qa1.md.
 - 2(b) the fullyCompletely.ownedRepository conditional, that the same probe would run there, that the rule is instructional for that session, and that QA1 must say so if it bears on a finding: all present.
 - 2(c) no "narrowest of the six" claim: the phrase survives in qa1.md only inside the sentence that disowns it as the first version's own overclaim, followed by the accurate comparison (Master Controller's default is equally narrow and never eligible for the broad grant). That is a correction, not a claim, and it is the right way to leave it.
 - "Name the asymmetry with LiveQA": satisfied in prose rather than by filename — the text contrasts the identical probe's DENIED result on QA1's profile with its running under LiveQA's, and says the rule is "exactly like LiveQA's own restraint" in the declared-owned case. The requirement asks for the asymmetry to be named, not for a file citation.
 - The amendment's own parenthetical is honest about why it exists and what it cost, which is the right shape for a post-PASS sprint-file change.
2. The new live criterion is exactly the third case I asked for in round 3: a headless QA1 in a project validly declaring fullyCompletely.ownedRepository in .claude/settings.local.json, where the probe should RUN rather than be denied, with the CLI version recorded. It names the correct file, consistent with the round-2 fix and with readOwnedRepositoryDeclaration's actual behaviour.
3. Unchanged and still true at 3471879: no permission grant moved (run-role.js is not in this sprint's diff at all), no version bump (package.json untouched across a08dbf5..3471879), Req 1/3/5 text as audited in rounds 1-3, and Req 6's two tests with the six plantings I ran across earlier rounds.

NOTHING OUTSTANDING. The Master Controller item I carried in rounds 1-3 (the sprint file's own premise overclaiming) is what this amendment closed.

FOR LIVEQA, unchanged from round 3 and now written into the sprint's own criteria: three probes, on the CLI version current at gate time, with that version recorded — default-profile QA1 denied, LiveQA runs, declared-owned QA1 runs. If any of the three has changed, the documentation is stale and needs its own correction rather than a pass.
